question: Bimbavati Devi is an exponent of which Indian dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipuri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bimbavati Devi is a renowned exponent of Manipuri dance, the classical dance form of Manipur. (मणिपुरी नृत्य — बिम्बावती देवी)

 

• She is the daughter of the legendary Manipuri dance guru Bipin Singh and Kalavati Devi, and has trained extensively under her father, carrying forward the Jhaveri sisters' and Bipin Singh's Manipuri repertoire.

 

• Manipuri dance is characterised by graceful, fluid movements, soft footwork, and themes drawn largely from Radha-Krishna (Raas Leela) episodes.

 

• It is one of the eight classical dance forms of India recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Raas Leela is the most prominent repertoire of Manipuri dance, performed in a circular formation depicting the divine love of Radha and Krishna.

 

• Other notable Manipuri dancers include Guru Bipin Singh, Darshana Jhaveri, and Nayana Jhaveri.

 

NOTE

 

• Chhau (Option 1): A semi-classical dance form of Odisha, Jharkhand and West Bengal, often martial in character.

 

• Kathakali (Option 3): A classical dance-drama from Kerala known for elaborate costumes and facial makeup.

 

• Odissi (Option 4): A classical dance form of Odisha, distinct from Manipuri in technique and repertoire.

question: It is the duty of every citizen to uphold and protect the ________, unity and integrity of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is sovereignty.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 51A(c) of the Fundamental Duties (Part IVA of the Constitution) states that it is the duty of every citizen of India to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India. (संप्रभुता, एकता और अखंडता — अनुच्छेद 51A)

 

• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

 

• Originally there were 10 Fundamental Duties; an 11th was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002, relating to providing education to children aged 6-14 years.

 

• Fundamental Duties are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR and, like the Directive Principles, are non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties are listed under Article 51A in Part IVA of the Constitution.

 

• They apply only to citizens, unlike Fundamental Rights, some of which extend to non-citizens as well.

 

NOTE

 

• autonomy (Option 1), authority (Option 2) and privacy (Option 4) do not appear anywhere in the text of Article 51A(c); the exact constitutional wording is "sovereignty, unity and integrity of India".

question:
Which of the following statements about the Vice President of India is INCORRECT?

1. Members of State legislatures do not take part in his elections.

2. He acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

3. The Vice President is elected for five years.

4. He can be removed from his office by the President approved through a resolution passed by the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
option_1: Members of State legislatures do not take part in his elections.
option_2: He acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
option_3: The Vice President is elected for five years.
option_4: He can be removed from his office by the President approved through a resolution passed by the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
solution_text:
The correct answer is He can be removed from his office by the President approved through a resolution passed by the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Article 67(b) of the Constitution, the Vice President may be removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha, passed by an effective majority and agreed to by the Lok Sabha by a simple majority. (उपराष्ट्रपति — निष्कासन प्रक्रिया)

 

• Crucially, this removal is a purely legislative process — it requires no assent or approval from the President, unlike what Statement 4 claims, which makes Statement 4 factually incorrect.

 

• Statement 1 is correct: The Vice President is elected by an electoral college consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, including nominated members); members of State legislatures do not participate.

 

• Statement 2 is correct: Under Article 64, the Vice President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: Under Article 66, the Vice President holds office for a term of five years, subject to earlier resignation or removal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Unlike the President's removal (impeachment under Article 61, which requires charges in one House and investigation/proof in the other), the Vice President's removal resolution requires no impeachment process and no presidential role.

 

• The current (as of December 2022) Vice President of India is Shri Jagdeep Dhankhar.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 are all constitutionally accurate statements about the Vice President and are therefore not the answer to this "INCORRECT statement" question.

question: The Kuchipudi classical dance is accompanied with which type of music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carnatic Music.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kuchipudi is a classical dance form that originated in the Kuchipudi village of Andhra Pradesh and is traditionally accompanied by Carnatic (South Indian classical) music. (कुचिपुड़ी नृत्य — कर्नाटक संगीत)

 

• It is a dance-drama performance, historically presented by all-male Brahmin troupes, and combines fast rhythmic footwork with graceful body movements and expressive abhinaya.

 

• It is one of the eight classical dance forms of India recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, along with Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

 

• The dance form is traditionally credited to the 17th-century Vaishnava saint-poet Siddhendra Yogi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu) and Mohiniyattam (Kerala) are also traditionally accompanied by Carnatic music.

 

• Kathak (North India), Odissi and Manipuri are generally associated with Hindustani music.

 

NOTE

 

• Kajri (Option 1): A folk-song genre of eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, sung during the monsoon, unrelated to Kuchipudi.

 

• Chaiti (Option 2): A folk-song genre associated with the Hindu month of Chaitra, also from the eastern UP-Bihar belt.

 

• Hindustani Music (Option 4): This is the North Indian classical tradition; Kuchipudi, being a South Indian form, is accompanied by Carnatic, not Hindustani, music.

question: Which Indian budget introduced a statement highlighting the gender sensitivities of the budgetary allocations?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2005-06.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gender Budgeting was formally introduced in India in the Union Budget of 2005-06, when a separate Gender Budget Statement (Statement 20/21) began to be presented as part of the budget documents. (लैंगिक बजट — 2005-06)

 

• The Gender Budget Statement shows the quantum of allocations for schemes that are wholly or substantially meant for women, split into Part A (100% women-specific) and Part B (at least 30% women-specific).

 

• The Ministry of Women and Child Development coordinates Gender Budgeting across ministries through Gender Budget Cells (GBCs) set up in various departments.

 

• Gender Budgeting is a tool of fiscal policy, not a separate budget, aimed at mainstreaming gender concerns into planning and resource allocation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's Gender Budgeting initiative was inspired by international precedents like Australia's 1984 women's budget statement.

 

• The Economic Survey and Union Budget both now regularly feature gender-related data and allocations.

 

NOTE

 

• 2008-09 (Option 1), 2010-11 (Option 2) and 2001-02 (Option 4) are all incorrect years — none of them mark the introduction of the Gender Budget Statement, which began with the 2005-06 budget.

question: According to Union Health Ministry, a new display image, with a warning written as “Tobacco causes painful death” will be printed on tobacco products manufactured, imported, or packaged on or after ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 December, 2022.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Union Health Ministry notified new, more graphic pictorial health warnings for tobacco product packaging, carrying the message "Tobacco causes painful death", to be printed on all tobacco products manufactured, imported or packaged on or after 1 December 2022. (तंबाकू चेतावनी — 1 दिसंबर 2022)

 

• The new warning images replaced the earlier set that had been in use since 2018, as mandated under the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA), 2003, and the associated Packaging and Labelling Rules.

 

• The health warning is required to cover 85% of the principal display area of tobacco packages (60% pictorial + 25% textual), split across the front and back panels.

 

• The notification was issued by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in mid-2022, giving manufacturers a transition period before the December 2022 effective date.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India ratified the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (FCTC) in 2004, which underpins such packaging and labelling regulations.

 

• Cigarette and tobacco packet warnings in India are periodically revised to keep public health messaging effective and prevent "warning fatigue".

 

NOTE

 

• 1 January 2023 (Option 1), 1 February 2023 (Option 2) and 1 November 2022 (Option 3) are all incorrect dates; the notified effective date was 1 December 2022.

question: Ishwarchandra vidyasagar set up school for girls at ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calcutta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, the noted Bengali social reformer and educationist, was instrumental in establishing schools for girls in Calcutta. (ईश्वर चंद्र विद्यासागर — कलकत्ता)

 

• He worked closely with John Elliot Drinkwater Bethune to establish the Bethune School in Calcutta in 1849, one of the earliest schools for girls' education in India.

 

• Vidyasagar also played a leading role in the passage of the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856, and campaigned against child marriage and polygamy.

 

• He is credited with modernising and simplifying the Bengali alphabet and prose style, and served as the principal of Sanskrit College, Calcutta.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vidyasagar helped open numerous girls' schools across Bengal during his tenure as a government school inspector in the 1850s.

 

• He is often referred to as "Vidyasagar" (Ocean of Knowledge), a title conferred for his scholarship in Sanskrit.

 

NOTE

 

• Bombay (Option 1), Surat (Option 2) and Lahore (Option 3) were not the centres of Vidyasagar's girls'-education work, which was based in and around Calcutta, Bengal.

question: The proposed Rowlett Act of 1919 allowed detention of political prisoners without trial for________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is two years.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rowlatt Act, 1919 (formally the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act) empowered the British government to arrest and detain political prisoners without trial for up to two years. (रॉलेट एक्ट — दो वर्ष तक बिना मुकदमे नज़रबंदी)

 

• It was based on the recommendations of the Rowlatt Committee, headed by British judge Sir Sidney Rowlatt, set up to examine revolutionary conspiracies.

 

• The Act allowed trial of political cases without juries and empowered provincial governments to intern suspects without judicial recourse, drawing widespread protest across India.

 

• Mahatma Gandhi launched the Rowlatt Satyagraha in 1919 in opposition, which was followed shortly by the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (13 April 1919) in Amritsar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Rowlatt Act was popularly dubbed the "Black Act" and the "No Dalil, No Vakil, No Appeal" Act for stripping away basic legal safeguards.

 

• The Jallianwala Bagh massacre, where General Dyer's troops fired on an unarmed crowd, is directly linked to the protests against the Rowlatt Act.

 

NOTE

 

• six months (Option 2), two months (Option 3) and one year (Option 4) all understate the actual detention period authorised by the Act, which was two years.

question: Which of the following is correctly matched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Loo - Hot wind.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Loo" refers to the strong, dry, dust-laden hot winds that blow during the day in the summer season (April-June) over the Indo-Gangetic plains of North and Northwest India. (लू — गर्म हवा)

 

• These winds typically blow from the west/northwest and can cause heat stroke and heat-related illnesses among people exposed to them.

 

• Kaal Baisakhi ("Nor'westers") are actually pre-monsoon thunderstorms accompanied by violent squalls, occurring in West Bengal and Assam during late afternoons in April-May, not "autumn winds".

 

• Trade winds are steady winds blowing from the subtropical high-pressure belts towards the equator; they are not associated with "winter snow storms".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kaal Baisakhi is locally called "Bardoli Chheerha" in Assam and is important for pre-monsoon tea and jute cultivation.

 

• In peninsular India, similar pre-monsoon local storms are called "mango showers" or "blossom showers" (in Kerala/Karnataka) and "Cherry blossom" showers (Coffee-growing areas).

 

NOTE

 

• Kaal Baisakhi - Autumn winds (Option 1): Incorrect; Kaal Baisakhi is a pre-monsoon (summer) thunderstorm, not an autumn wind.

 

• Trade winds - Winter snow storm (Option 2): Incorrect; trade winds are tropical wind belts unrelated to snow storms.

 

• Loo - Winter stormy winds (Option 4): Incorrect; Loo blows in summer, not winter, and is a hot dry wind, not a storm.

question: The scheme, “Bahini”, aims at providing 100 percent access to free and safe sanitary pads to secondary and senior secondary school going girls. This scheme was launched by which state government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sikkim.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The "Bahini" scheme was launched by the Government of Sikkim to provide 100% access to free and safe sanitary pads to girl students in secondary and senior secondary schools (Classes 9-12). (बहिनी योजना — सिक्किम)

 

• It was the first such comprehensive state-wide scheme in India covering all girl students of these classes, aimed at reducing school dropouts caused by lack of menstrual hygiene facilities.

 

• The scheme built upon a 2018 pilot programme run with Sulabh International, which installed sanitary pad vending machines in select Sikkim schools.

 

• Objectives of the scheme include improving menstrual hygiene awareness and ensuring uninterrupted school attendance for girls during menstruation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sikkim's Chief Minister at the time was Prem Singh Tamang ("P.S. Golay").

 

• Sikkim also runs the "Aama" (mother) scheme, a related welfare initiative for mothers, announced around the same period.

 

NOTE

 

• Bihar (Option 1), Arunachal Pradesh (Option 3) and Assam (Option 4) did not launch the Bahini scheme; it is specific to Sikkim.

question: The Competition (Amendment) Bill, 2022 proposes to reduce the timeline for the CCI to pass an order on transactions from 210 days to _______ days.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 150.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Competition (Amendment) Bill, 2022 proposes to reduce the time limit for the Competition Commission of India (CCI) to pass an order approving or rejecting a combination (merger/acquisition) from 210 days to 150 days. (प्रतिस्पर्धा संशोधन विधेयक — 150 दिन)

 

• The Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha in August 2022 to amend the Competition Act, 2002, and was subsequently referred to a Parliamentary Standing Committee.

 

• The amendment aims to make the merger-approval process faster and more business-friendly, reducing regulatory delays for companies.

 

• The Bill also introduces changes such as a deal-value threshold for notifying combinations and reduces the timeline for prima facie opinion formation by CCI from 30 to 20 working days.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Competition Act, 2002 replaced the earlier MRTP Act, 1969, and the CCI is the statutory body responsible for enforcing competition law in India.

 

• The amended Act was eventually passed as the Competition (Amendment) Act, 2023.

 

NOTE

 

• 140 (Option 1), 180 (Option 2) and 190 (Option 4) are all incorrect figures; the Bill specifies a reduction to 150 days.

question: At present, the Grand Trunk Road extends from __________ in India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amritsar to Kolkata.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At present, within India, the Grand Trunk (GT) Road extends from Amritsar (Punjab) to Kolkata (West Bengal), forming part of National Highway 19 (formerly NH-2). (ग्रांड ट्रंक रोड — अमृतसर से कोलकाता)

 

• Historically, the GT Road was one of Asia's oldest and longest roads, originally extending from Kabul (Afghanistan) to Chittagong (Bangladesh), and was developed/renovated by Sher Shah Suri in the 16th century.

 

• It passes through major cities including Amritsar, Delhi, Kanpur, Allahabad (Prayagraj), Varanasi and Kolkata.

 

• The road is also historically known as "Sadak-e-Azam", "Badshahi Sadak", and "Uttarapatha" in different periods.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sher Shah Suri is credited with major renovation of the route, including planting trees and building sarais (rest houses) along it.

 

• The GT Road today is a key part of India's National Highway network connecting the northwest to the east.

 

NOTE

 

• Kashmir to Kanyakumari (Option 1) describes the north-south corridor of India's highway network, not the GT Road.

 

• Chennai to Kolkata (Option 3) and Agra to Kolkata (Option 4) do not correctly describe the present extent of the GT Road within India, which runs from Amritsar to Kolkata.

question: What is the average circumference of the standard cricket ball in international cricket?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8.81 inches - 9 inches.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per ICC (International Cricket Council) regulations, a standard cricket ball must have a circumference between 8.81 inches (22.4 cm) and 9 inches (22.9 cm), roughly corresponding to 224 mm to 229 mm. (क्रिकेट गेंद परिधि — 8.81 से 9 इंच)

 

• The weight of the ball is specified as between 155.9 grams (5.5 oz) and 163 grams (5.75 oz).

 

• Cricket balls are made of cork covered by leather stitched together with a prominent seam of six rows of stitching.

 

• Ball specifications differ slightly by format and gender category (men's/women's, and junior cricket uses smaller/lighter balls).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cricket balls are typically red (Test/First-class cricket), white (limited-overs/day-night matches) or pink (day-night Test matches).

 

• The seam of the ball plays a major role in enabling swing and seam bowling.

 

NOTE

 

• 7.89-8.45 inches (Option 1), 10.46-10.90 inches (Option 2) and 9.45-10.20 inches (Option 3) all fall outside the ICC-specified range of 8.81-9 inches for a standard cricket ball.

question: Which of the following festivals is known as Vijaya Utsav?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hampi Festival.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Hampi Festival, also known as "Vijaya Utsav" or "Hampi Utsav", is an annual three-day festival held at Hampi, Karnataka, celebrating the glory of the Vijayanagara Empire. (हम्पी उत्सव — विजय उत्सव)

 

• It is organised by the Government of Karnataka at the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Hampi, the former capital of the Vijayanagara Empire.

 

• The festival features dance, music, puppet shows, fireworks, and processions, showcasing the region's rich cultural and historical legacy.

 

• It usually takes place in November each year, drawing artists and tourists from across the country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hampi was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, founded by Harihara and Bukka in the 14th century.

 

• The Virupaksha Temple and the Stone Chariot at the Vittala Temple are iconic monuments at Hampi.

 

NOTE

 

• Gangasagar Mela (Option 2): A major Hindu pilgrimage fair held at Sagar Island, West Bengal, on Makar Sankranti.

 

• Pushkar Fair (Option 3): An annual camel and livestock fair held at Pushkar, Rajasthan.

 

• Konark Dance Festival (Option 4): An annual classical dance festival held near the Sun Temple at Konark, Odisha.

question: The type of forests located in mid latitudinal coastal region is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Temperate evergreen forest.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Temperate evergreen forests are typically found in the mid-latitudinal coastal regions of continents, where moderate rainfall and temperature prevail throughout the year. (शीतोष्ण सदाबहार वन — मध्य अक्षांशीय तटीय क्षेत्र)

 

• These forests consist mainly of hardwood trees such as oak, eucalyptus, and evergreen broadleaf species, adapted to mild, moist climatic conditions.

 

• Examples of such regions include parts of south-east Australia, south Chile, south-east Brazil, natal (South Africa), and coastal parts of China and Japan.

 

• They differ from temperate deciduous forests, which shed leaves in winter and are typically found further inland/higher latitude with a more continental climate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Monsoon forests (tropical deciduous) are found in regions with distinct wet and dry seasons, like most of peninsular India.

 

• Mediterranean vegetation (evergreen scrub/hardwood forest) is found in regions with the Mediterranean climate — dry summers and mild wet winters — typically at slightly lower (subtropical) latitudes than temperate evergreen forests.

 

NOTE

 

• Tropical rainforest (Option 1): Found near the equator, characterised by heavy year-round rainfall, not mid-latitude coasts.

 

• Mediterranean vegetation (Option 2): Associated with the Mediterranean-type climate at subtropical latitudes (e.g., around the Mediterranean Sea, California), distinct from the mid-latitude coastal temperate evergreen belt.

 

• Monsoon forest (Option 3): A tropical/subtropical deciduous forest type driven by monsoon rainfall patterns, not specifically a mid-latitude coastal formation.

question: When did Prime Minister, Narendra Modi integrate selected fitness enthusiasts of the country in the first session of ‘Fit India Dialogue’ as a part of the ‘Fit India Movement’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 24 September 2020.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Prime Minister Narendra Modi interacted with selected fitness enthusiasts from across the country in the first session of the ‘Fit India Dialogue’ on 24 September 2020, marking the first anniversary of the Fit India Movement. (फिट इंडिया संवाद — 24 सितंबर 2020)

 

• The Fit India Movement was originally launched by PM Modi on 29 August 2019 (National Sports Day) to encourage citizens to incorporate fitness and physical activity into their daily lives.

 

• The Fit India Dialogue session featured interactions with fitness influencers, yoga practitioners, and sportspersons on ways to promote health and fitness across India.

 

• The initiative is run under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Fit India Movement logo and tagline emphasise "Fitness ki Dose, Aadha Ghanta Roz" (a dose of fitness, half an hour daily).

 

• National Sports Day is celebrated on 29 August, the birth anniversary of hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand.

 

NOTE

 

• 24 September 2019 (Option 1), 24 September 2018 (Option 2) and 24 September 2021 (Option 4) are incorrect years; the first Fit India Dialogue session was held on 24 September 2020.

question: Which of the following is the most important festival celebrated by the Muslim community in India to mark the beginning of the Islamic New Year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Muharram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Muharram is the first month of the Islamic (Hijri) calendar, and its observance marks the beginning of the Islamic New Year. (मुहर्रम — इस्लामी नववर्ष)

 

• For Shia Muslims in particular, the 10th day of Muharram (Ashura) commemorates the martyrdom of Imam Hussain, grandson of Prophet Muhammad, at the Battle of Karbala.

 

• The occasion is observed with mourning processions, recitations, and, in some places, the taking out of tazias (replicas of Hussain's tomb).

 

• The Islamic calendar is a lunar calendar, so Muharram (and other Islamic festivals) shifts earlier each year relative to the Gregorian calendar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Eid-ul-Fitr marks the end of the fasting month of Ramzan (Ramadan).

 

• Eid-ul-Zuha (Bakrid) commemorates the willingness of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) to sacrifice his son, and involves the sacrifice of an animal.

 

NOTE

 

• Milad-Un-Nabi (Option 1): Celebrates the birthday of Prophet Muhammad, not the new year.

 

• Idu’l Zuha (Option 3): Commemorates Prophet Ibrahim's sacrifice; observed in the month of Dhu al-Hijjah, not at the year's start.

 

• Idu’l Fitr (Option 4): Marks the end of Ramzan fasting, in the month of Shawwal, not the Islamic New Year.

question: In which of the following years was the Treaty of Salbai signed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1782.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Treaty of Salbai was signed in 1782 between the British East India Company (represented by Warren Hastings) and the Marathas (represented by Mahadji Scindia on behalf of Peshwa Madhav Rao II). (सालबाई की संधि — 1782)

 

• It formally ended the First Anglo-Maratha War (1775-1782), which had begun over disputes involving the succession to the Peshwaship.

 

• Under the treaty, the British retained Salsette Island, and the treaty ensured about 20 years of peace between the British and the Marathas.

 

• The treaty also secured Maratha neutrality for the British against Mysore's Hyder Ali, indirectly aiding the British in the Second Anglo-Mysore War.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mahadji Scindia played a key mediating role in the negotiations leading up to the Treaty of Salbai.

 

• The Second Anglo-Maratha War broke out later, in 1803-1805, ending the relatively long peace established by this treaty.

 

NOTE

 

• 1817 (Option 1) is associated with the start of the Third Anglo-Maratha War, not the Treaty of Salbai.

 

• 1769 (Option 2) and 1800 (Option 3) do not correspond to the signing of the Treaty of Salbai, which took place in 1782.

question: Limestone, chalk and marble are different forms of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calcium carbonate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Limestone, chalk and marble are all naturally occurring forms of calcium carbonate (CaCO3), differing mainly in their geological formation and crystalline structure. (कैल्शियम कार्बोनेट — चूना पत्थर, खड़िया, संगमरमर)

 

• Limestone is a sedimentary rock formed largely from marine organism shells and skeletal fragments composed of calcite.

 

• Chalk is a soft, fine-grained, porous form of limestone formed from the calcareous shells of microscopic marine organisms like foraminifera.

 

• Marble is formed by the metamorphism (recrystallisation) of limestone under heat and pressure, giving it a crystalline texture.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Heating calcium carbonate produces calcium oxide (quicklime) and carbon dioxide; adding water to calcium oxide gives calcium hydroxide (slaked lime).

 

• Calcium carbonate is also the main constituent of coral and mollusc shells, and is used industrially in cement manufacturing.

 

NOTE

 

• Calcium phosphate (Option 1): The main mineral component of bones and teeth, not limestone/chalk/marble.

 

• Calcium hydroxide (Option 2): Known as slaked lime, produced by treating quicklime with water — a derivative, not the base rock form.

 

• Calcium oxide (Option 3): Known as quicklime, produced by heating limestone — again a derivative product, not the natural rock itself.

question: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding king Harshavardhana?
option_1: Harshavardhana ruled nearly about 1400 years ago
option_2: Xuan Zang spent a lot of time at Harsha’s court
option_3: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Hari'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/HARI.TTF') format('truetype');} </style>Harshavardhana’s court poet was Harishena
option_4: Harshacharita is a biography written on Harshavardhana
solution_text:
The correct answer is Harshavardhana's court poet was Harishena.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Harshavardhana's court poet was Banabhatta, not Harishena — this makes the statement in Option 3 factually incorrect. (हर्षवर्धन का राजकवि — बाणभट्ट, हरिषेण नहीं)

 

• Harishena was actually the court poet of the Gupta emperor Samudragupta, and is famous as the author of the Allahabad Prashasti (Prayaga Prashasti) inscribed on the Ashokan pillar at Allahabad.

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Harshavardhana ruled from 606 to 647 CE, which is roughly 1400 years before the present day.

 

• Statement 2 is correct: The Chinese Buddhist traveller Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang) visited India during Harsha's reign and spent considerable time at his court, later documenting his travels in Si-Yu-Ki.

 

• Statement 4 is correct: Harshacharita, written by Banabhatta, is a biographical account of Harshavardhana's life and reign.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Harshavardhana ruled from his capital at Kannauj and is also credited with authoring Sanskrit plays such as Ratnavali, Priyadarshika and Nagananda.

 

• Harsha convened a famous religious assembly at Kannauj to honour Xuanzang and promote Buddhism.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are all factually accurate statements about Harshavardhana and hence not the answer to this "NOT correct" question.

question: For the first time the objective of self-reliance was incorporated in the ____ Five-Year Plan.
solution_text:
The correct answer is third.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The objective of self-reliance (Atmanirbharta) for the Indian economy was, for the first time, formally incorporated as a goal in the Third Five-Year Plan (1961-1966). (आत्मनिर्भरता — तृतीय पंचवर्षीय योजना)

 

• The Third Plan aimed to make the economy self-reliant and self-generating, focusing on establishing a strong industrial and agricultural base to reduce dependence on foreign aid/imports.

 

• However, the Third Plan is often regarded as a relative failure due to the Sino-Indian War (1962), the Indo-Pak War (1965), and a severe drought (1965-66), which diverted resources and disrupted planning priorities.

 

• The failures of the Third Plan led to a "Plan Holiday" (1966-69), during which annual plans were implemented instead of a Five-Year Plan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model and focused on agriculture.

 

• The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61), based on the Mahalanobis model, emphasised rapid industrialisation, especially heavy industry.

 

NOTE

 

• second (Option 2), fifth (Option 3) and first (Option 4) did not first introduce the self-reliance objective; it was the Third Five-Year Plan that did so.

question: Productivity of an ecosystem is composed of which of the following?
option_4: Net primary productivity and gross primary productivity
solution_text:
The correct answer is Net primary productivity and gross primary productivity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The primary productivity of an ecosystem is broadly composed of Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) and Net Primary Productivity (NPP). (सकल एवं शुद्ध प्राथमिक उत्पादकता)

 

• Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) is the total rate of organic matter production (via photosynthesis) by producers (plants/algae) in an ecosystem.

 

• Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is the GPP minus the energy lost to respiration (R) by the producers themselves, i.e., NPP = GPP - R; it represents the energy actually available for consumption by heterotrophs (herbivores, etc.).

 

• These two together represent the total "productivity" framework used to measure an ecosystem's energy capture and availability.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Secondary productivity refers to the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers (heterotrophs), distinct from primary productivity.

 

• Productivity is usually expressed in units such as g/m²/yr (grams per square metre per year) of biomass or kcal/m²/yr.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 mix up or misstate the correct terminology; the standard ecological classification of an ecosystem's (primary) productivity is into gross primary productivity and net primary productivity.

question: How does hydrochloric acid help in facilitating the action of pepsin?
option_1: Hydrochloric acid creates an acidic medium which facilitates the action of the enzyme pepsin.
option_2: Hydrochloric acid helps break down pepsin.
option_3: Hydrochloric acid creates an alkaline medium which facilitates the action of the enzyme pepsin.
option_4: Hydrochloric acid creates a basic medium which facilitates the action of the enzyme pepsin.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hydrochloric acid creates an acidic medium which facilitates the action of the enzyme pepsin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hydrochloric acid (HCl), secreted by the gastric (oxyntic/parietal) glands in the stomach lining, creates a strongly acidic medium (pH around 1.5-2) that is essential for the proper functioning of the enzyme pepsin. (हाइड्रोक्लोरिक अम्ल — अम्लीय माध्यम, पेप्सिन)

 

• Pepsin is a proteolytic (protein-digesting) enzyme that works optimally in this acidic environment to break down dietary proteins into smaller peptides.

 

• HCl also converts the inactive enzyme precursor pepsinogen (secreted by chief/peptic cells) into its active form, pepsin.

 

• Additionally, the acidic medium created by HCl helps kill ingested bacteria and pathogens, providing a protective/antiseptic function.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The stomach's mucosal lining is protected from this acid by a thick layer of mucus secreted by goblet cells.

 

• Other digestive enzymes, like salivary amylase, work best in a near-neutral medium and become inactive in the stomach's acidic environment.

 

NOTE

 

• Hydrochloric acid helps break down pepsin (Option 2): Incorrect; HCl activates pepsin (from pepsinogen) and provides its working medium — it does not break pepsin down.

 

• alkaline medium (Option 3) and basic medium (Option 4): Both incorrect; HCl creates an acidic, not alkaline/basic, medium in the stomach.

question: In 1979, who shared the Nobel Prize with Georg Wittig for their ‘development of the use of boron- and phosphorus-containing compounds, respectively, into important reagents in organic synthesis’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Herbert C Brown.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 1979 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was jointly awarded to Herbert C. Brown and Georg Wittig "for their development of the use of boron- and phosphorus-containing compounds, respectively, into important reagents in organic synthesis". (नोबेल रसायन पुरस्कार 1979 — हर्बर्ट सी ब्राउन)

 

• Herbert C. Brown is credited with developing hydroboration — a key reaction using organoboron compounds in organic synthesis.

 

• Georg Wittig is known for developing the Wittig reaction, which uses phosphorus ylides to convert aldehydes/ketones into alkenes.

 

• This shared prize honoured complementary breakthroughs that greatly expanded the toolbox of synthetic organic chemistry.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Herbert C. Brown was an American chemist born in London, known for pioneering work on boranes and organoboranes.

 

• The Wittig reaction, named after Georg Wittig, remains a fundamental method for forming carbon-carbon double bonds.

 

NOTE

 

• Arne Tiselius (Option 2): Won the 1948 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for research on electrophoresis and adsorption analysis, particularly serum proteins.

 

• Henry Taube (Option 3): Won the 1983 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for work on electron transfer mechanisms in metal complexes.

 

• Emil Fischer (Option 4): Won the 1902 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for work on sugar and purine syntheses; none of these three shared the 1979 prize with Wittig.

question: According to census 2011, the male literacy rate in India is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 82.14 percent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India, 2011, the male literacy rate in India was 82.14 percent, while the female literacy rate was 65.46 percent. (जनगणना 2011 — पुरुष साक्षरता दर 82.14%)

 

• The overall literacy rate of India as per Census 2011 was 74.04 percent, up from 64.83% in Census 2001.

 

• Kerala recorded the highest literacy rate among Indian states (93.91%), while Bihar recorded the lowest (61.80%).

 

• The Census 2011 was India's 15th National Census, conducted under the Ministry of Home Affairs, with Census Day marked as 1 March 2011.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The gender gap in literacy (male minus female) narrowed from earlier censuses but still stood at around 16.68 percentage points in 2011.

 

• Census 2011 recorded India's total population as approximately 121 crore (1.21 billion).

 

NOTE

 

• 81.14 percent (Option 1), 84.14 percent (Option 3) and 83.14 percent (Option 4) are all incorrect figures; the precise Census 2011 male literacy rate was 82.14 percent.
